newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICAN CRICKET BOARD RECOGNISES ONLY WIVES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICAN CRICKET BOARD RECOGNISES ONLY WIVES.

text.p: The United Cricket Board of South Africa (UCBSA) has upset some of its senior players on the eve the first test match against India by announcing that only wives and not girlfriends would be flown to Durban for the Christmas test.
"It is not a question of not allowing the girlfriends at all. It is a question of who pays what", UCBSA managing director Ali Bacher told Reuters.
In the past the UCBSA has appeared to handle the difficult issue of wives, girlfriends and tours successfully.

The cost of the wives' and girlfriends' visit to the team on their tour of India last month was divided between the UCBSA and the players. It was mutually agreed that children would not be included and the visits were only to be during the time of the Amedabad and Calcutta tests.
The visits were heralded as a great success by the players and UCBSA alike.
Captain Hansie Cronje said in a television interview after the South African victory in Calcutta: "It was great to do it (win) in front of our wives and girlfriends".
However, the UCBSA has now changed its mind when it comes to unmarried players.

"It is a change of policy in regard to payment but we are not saying to the unmarried guys that their girlfriends cannot be there. If they feel the presence of their girlfriend enhances their performance we will not stop them." explained Bacher.

Vice-captain Gary Kirsten, who is unmarried, said: "I am disappointed. I feel strongly that wives and girlfriends should be treated as one. To have them with us gives us emotional stability. At special times of the year you want special people to be with you on an 'official' basis!"
